answer: A concrete defense is compute-work identity attestation: each agent must spend verifiable compute and lock a non-transferable bond before it may vote or transact. Peers co-sign only after replaying that work, so every newcomer carries a permanent onyx record instead of a disposable alias. A rotating beacon publishes fresh randomness that reassigns reviewers each round, making pre-farmed identities costly. The relic of each attestation stays on-chain, so sybils cannot conceal their shared origin. An attacker pays real energy, locked capital, and public exposure for each extra identity.
